findings.element: .b-measure[data-across="true"] .b-item[data-lead="true"] .b-tick — the one accent-filled mark on the horizontal measure. Broken by [data-app="timeline"][data-medium="sheet"|"full"] .b-item[data-lead="true"] .b-tick { left: -28px } at _gate-suite.html:7785-7786, which outranks [data-app="timeline"] .b-measure[data-across="true"] .b-tick { left: 0; transform: translate(-50%,-50%) } at :8297
findings.problem: Direction B's whole claim is that position on the measure is daysFromToday x pixels-per-day computed from real dates. On the ACROSS axis the one mark the design accents as "this one, next" is the only mark plotted at the wrong distance. Measured at 1920x1000 (?layout=across): the .b-item for 'Menu tasting at The Orchard / Sat 1 Aug / 16' anchors at x=524.5, and its title, its date, its '16' and its own stem (.b-item::after, left:0) all sit at 524.5 — but its .b-tick centre is at 496.5, exactly 28.0px left. Every other tick is dead on (dx=0.0 at days 23, 37, 44, 51, 65, 79), so the filled dot visibly detaches from the stem that points at it. Cause is specificity: the desk-medium lead override is (0,5,0) and beats the across-axis rule at (0,4,0), so `left: 0` reaches all six ordinary marks and never the lead one. 28px is not a fixed error in days, because the rail rescales: 1602px/79d at 1920 reads 1.4 days early, 1.97 early at 1440, 2.30 at 1280, and 4.73 days early at 768 (rail 468px/79d), where the mark for Sat 1 August lands where Monday 27 July belongs. Identical on paper and on ink. The DOWN axis is correct (every tick dx=-23.5), so the error appears only on the axis whose entire job is horizontal distance — and both gates pass because neither compares a tick's centre with its item's anchor.
findings.fix: Add one rule after _gate-suite.html:8300 so the across axis governs the lead mark as it already governs the other six: `[data-app="timeline"] .b-measure[data-across="true"] .b-item[data-lead="true"] .b-tick { left: 0; }` — (0,5,0) and later in the file, so it beats :7786. If you would rather not stack a counter-rule, scope both desk overrides to the vertical axis instead by inserting `.b-measure:not([data-across="true"])` after the [data-medium] compound at :7781-7782 and :7785-7786, which leaves the down axis byte-identical. Then close the hole in the gate: for every .b-item on the across measure assert |tick centre x - item anchor x| <= 0.5px.

findings.element: [data-app="tasks"] .board > section.tray > article.card .cardTitle / .cardNote, with .drawer open — [data-app="tasks"]:has(.drawer) .sheet { margin-right: calc(364px + var(--inset)) } at _gate-suite.html:3421, against the lane floor `repeat(5, minmax(258px, 1fr))` that exists only inside @media (max-width: 1099px) at :3412-3413
findings.problem: This is the paid-for library's "the measure has a floor AND a ceiling" defect, back with the same trigger and almost the same number. Drove Planning open at 1440x960: the sheet goes 1322 -> 916, lanes go 280 -> 196, the card goes 256 -> 172 and .cardNote's measure goes 202px -> 118px — about 17 characters a line. Counted the damage: with the drawer shut, 0 of 13 card titles and 0 of 13 notes are clipped; with it open, 4 of 13 titles clip ('Reprint the faded welcome sign before the open...', 'Send midweek rate to the June 2027 walk-in...', 'Clear Sunday 11am late checkout...', 'Send registrar paperwork two...') and 'Menu tasting at The Orchard' loses its note's operative clause to the five-line cap, while its 27-character title now breaks over three lines. Same at 1280 (sheet 756, note 118px). Orla opens Planning to plan against the board, and the act of opening it takes a third of the board's words away. The trims themselves are clean — whole-word, full string in the aria-label — so nothing is lied about; the composition just stops being legible at a width no frame covers. The floor that fixes it is already written in this file, 9 lines above the drawer rule, keyed to a viewport query the drawer can never trigger.
findings.fix: Apply the existing lane floor whenever the SHEET is narrow, not just when the window is. measureEdges already stamps `data-head="stack"` on the sheet at `sheet.clientWidth < 1200` (_gate-suite.html:15261) precisely because the drawer, not the viewport, is what narrows it — so reuse that stamp: add `[data-app="tasks"] .sheet[data-head="stack"] .board { grid-template-columns: repeat(5, minmax(258px, 1fr)); }`. At 1440 drawer-open the sheet is 916, the board's scrollWidth becomes ~1290 against 884 of viewport and the board scrolls with the snap that is already on .tray/.tray:last-child and already gate-proven ('Done is still on the board'). Lanes return to 258, the note measure to ~181px, and 0 of 13 titles clip. This also covers the 1100-1199 window band, where the same floor is missing today (lanes 203px, a second lane head wrapping).

findings.element: header.tlHead > span.word ("timeline") — [data-app="timeline"] .tlHead { padding: 40px 40px 0 }, against .head { height: 60px; padding: 0 28px } for tasks and .head { padding: 10px 30px } for notes
findings.problem: The suite's argument is that nothing rebuilds when you cross the rail, and the wordmark on the sheet's own head is the object that proves it. It does not hold still. Clicked .rail [data-rail="notes|tasks|timeline"] round-trip at 1920x1000 and re-measured span.word on every crossing (stable and repeatable): box top y=37.0 for tasks and y=38.1 for notes — the two agree to 1.1px — and y=58.0 for timeline. Timeline's word also sits on 25.5px leading against 22px and 21.76px, so its baseline lands 22.8px lower and the box bottom moves 59.0 / 59.9 / 83.5. Same family, same 17px, same weight 600: nothing but padding puts it there. Clicking Timeline visibly drops the identity and clicking back lifts it, which is the one motion the architecture promises will not happen. The same padding also spends a 66px band on one 70px word and then builds a second head (div.b-bar, 56px, carrying the project name and the three acts) 40px beneath it, where tasks and notes carry identity, project, facts and actions on one 60-62px line. The horizontal difference (128 / 471 / 140) is defensible — each wordmark aligns to its own product's measure. The vertical is aligned to nothing.
findings.fix: Land it on the line the other two already share: `[data-app="timeline"] .tlHead { height: 60px; padding: 19px 40px 0; }` and `[data-app="timeline"] .tlHead .word { line-height: 22px; }`. That puts the box top at y=37 and the leading at 22px — pixel-identical to tasks, within 1.1px of notes — and lifts the stage 6px, which nothing below depends on. Then assert it: span.word's bounding top must agree within 1.5px across the three data-rail crossings at 1920, 1440 and 1280.

findings.element: section.tray[data-lane="waiting"] > .trayHead > .trayNote, sized by [data-app="tasks"] .board:has(> .tray[data-lane="waiting"][data-empty]) { --col-waiting: var(--rail) } at _gate-suite.html:1789 (--rail: minmax(132px,172px))
findings.problem: The empty lane yielding its width is a decision, stated in the comment at :1782. The prose staying full-width inside the yielded track is not. Measured at 1920x1000: To do / In progress / Review / Done are 372px each, their .trayNote sits on one 17px line, .trayHead is 50px, and all four first cards start at y=197. Waiting is pinned to 172px, so 'Held by a reply, a delivery, or a decision.' wraps to two lines (34px), its .trayHead is 67px, and its only content starts at y=227 — 30px below the four cards beside it. Constant at 1680, 1440 and 1280 (172px every time), and worse with Planning open at 1440: Waiting drops to 132px with a THREE-line note (head 83px, content at y=344) while Review wraps to two (head 67px, y=314) and the rest hold 50px/298 — three head heights and three first-row baselines in one five-lane row, spanning 46px. The proof that it is fallout and not intent: the phone board, where every lane is 299px, renders all five notes on one line with all five heads at 50px, and the tasks.dense state at 1920, where Waiting is populated and its note fits one line at 372px. The row of five lane heads is the strongest horizontal line on the board, and it is the one line that does not hold.
findings.fix: Stop the yielded lane carrying body prose in its head. Add beside the five --col rules at :1786-1790: `[data-app="tasks"] .board:not([data-filtered]):not([data-blank]) > .tray[data-empty] .trayNote { display: none; }`, and move the sentence into the empty body so nothing is lost — render .trayEmpty as "Nothing held up. This lane holds anything waiting on a reply, a delivery or a decision.", which is the lane's only content and can wrap freely. All five .trayHead boxes then measure 50px and all five first rows start on one baseline at every width; the lane floor in the drawer-crushes-the-card-measure fix covers the remaining wrap on Review.

findings.element: [data-app="tasks"] .lrow { align-items: center } at _gate-suite.html:1611, overriding [data-app="tasks"] .lrows { align-items: start } at :1600 — the default view below 1100 and the phone's only view
findings.problem: The row is a five-column subgrid in which one column is top-aligned and four float to the row's vertical middle, so a row has no shared first line. Measured on row one ('Confirm marquee sides with the hire company' + a three-line note) at 768x1024: .lrowTitle's first line centres at y=241.8, while .tick, .lrowLane ('TO DO'), .lrowWho ('Mara & Finn') and .lrowMeta all centre at y=280.5 — 38.7px lower, level with line two of the note. The offset is a function of note length, not a constant: 38.7px on that row, 20.3px on a two-line row at 1050, 0px on a single-line row, and 38.7px for the tick at 390. So the leftmost column of the list — thirteen circles down the page — wobbles by up to 39px against the titles they tick, and reading across a row you pass a title, then a note, then meet the lane and the owner two lines below where the row began. It is also the one alignment declaration in this file with no comment defending it. Nothing here needs invention: the parent already declares `align-items: start`.
findings.fix: Two lines. `[data-app="tasks"] .lrow { align-items: start; }` at :1611, and `[data-app="tasks"] .lrow .lrowLane { margin-top: 2px; }`. The measured heights make the rest free: .tick is 18.0px against a 17.92px first line, so it lands on the title with no compensation, and .lrowWho / .lrowMeta are 17px, within half a pixel. The phone keeps its designed two-row grid — .lrowLane stays on grid-row 2 (:1690 band) and simply starts at that row's top. Assert it: in every .lrow, the centre of .tick must sit within 2px of the centre of .lrowTitle's first line at 1050, 768 and 390.

biggestWin: One centre axis, honoured by every major object in all three products, so crossing the rail never re-centres the page. At 1920 the sheet's centre is x=1001, and the notes head, the paper stack, the index, the review card and its three ghost layers (symmetric to 0.1px), the dock capsule, the timeline stage (40px inset both sides) and the dictation transcript all centre on it to within 1px. The dictation floor's corner insets are exact — 32px left at the top, 32px left at the foot, 32px right at the foot — with a deliberate 26/34 top-to-bottom compensation that reads as centred rather than measuring as centred. And the populated board (tasks.dense at 1920) is the real proof of the grid: five equal 372px lanes, five one-line lane notes, five first cards on y=197, one baseline. Every defect above is a mechanical fault in a surface whose composition is otherwise held to the pixel — a specificity collision, a padding value, a missing floor, an empty-state cascade and one align-items. Nothing here needs a build or a different decision; it needs one polish pass, and the largest of the five is a truth defect on the timeline's own organising claim rather than a matter of taste.
